constraints.text: A bare majority. The PAICV won 37 of the 72 National Assembly seats (48.04% of the vote) and the MpD kept 33 (44.75%). Thirty-seven is exactly the majority line, so the new government has no margin for a lost vote in the house; turnout was 46.5%.

constraints.text: Opposition on the other side of a near-even split. The MpD, which had sought a third term for Ulisses Correia e Silva, keeps 33 seats and nearly 45% of the vote, so each foreign or fiscal decision will be argued in the house at close quarters.

paradoxes.text: Courting Portuguese investors to carry the diversification plan ties the economy to the former metropole's capital, while the new government promises a 'new Cape Verde' with a role for all islands. Our reading (confidence C): the Lisbon channel is what the sources show, and the promise is about the archipelago's own economy, so the two may pull apart.

grand_strategy.reading: Cape Verde's 17 May 2026 election ended the MpD's bid for a third term: the PAICV won 37 of 72 seats, and Francisco Carvalho was named prime minister-designate, with 19 June given as the swearing-in date by one search summary that no second source confirmed. The state's external ties that the sources read here run through Lisbon (the AIR Centre and Portuguese investment), with China and the United States present but not sourced in this pass. The EU, ECOWAS, Brazil and the CPLP, the Chinese port and debt, the MCC compacts and the remittance and tourism figures are open gaps for a second pass.

stances.note: Former metropole and Lusophone partner, cooperating on investment and research without a treaty. The AIR Centre (founded 2017, Cabo Verde a founding partner) and Prime Minister Montenegro's April 2024 visit urging Portuguese investment make the cooperation partner-like, not alignment. Confidence C: the grade is our reading from two sources, and the bond kin (shared Portuguese language and colonial history) is our reading too; no source read names the bond. Trend stable: no 2025-2026 Portugal-Cabo Verde source was read. Mirrored: the Portugal row toward Cabo Verde (visit, April 2024) from data/relations/PRT.yaml, same sources.

stances.note: Transactional partner. Relations date from 25 April 1976 (Wikipedia, citation not checked); the Chinese statement of 2006 calls China a friend since before independence and cites trade of about US$1.8 million in 2002. The grade rests on that statement, which is state-agency material (tier 1 for the statement only, not for the facts), plus the trade figure it gives. Bond affinity: the friendship is the government's own framing, with no kinship. Not sourced in this pass: the Chinese port, the debt and any 2025-2026 visit. Trend stable is our reading; no source gives a direction.
